markers.title: "Channel" column header mismatches its data
markers.body: The first column is labelled 'Channel' but every row underneath (Double Room, Standard Twin, Budget Studio…) is a room type or rate plan, not a distribution channel. Relabel the header to match whichever filter is active (e.g. 'Room type'), or update it dynamically when the filter changes.

markers.title: Header controls under the 44dp tap minimum
markers.body: The 'Bulk update' button, and the Room types / Rate plans / Channels filter chips below it, all render at 32dp tall — 12dp short of the iOS HIG minimum. Increase vertical padding on all of them.

markers.title: Rate/availability cells have no editable affordance
markers.body: This is a rates & availabilities management screen, but the number cells (e.g. '240', '5') look like static text — no border, icon, or tap state hints they're editable. Add a visible edit affordance (underline, pencil icon, or tap highlight) if they're meant to be tapped.

markers.title: Wide rate table has no horizontal-scroll affordance
markers.body: The date grid extends far beyond the 390dp viewport (14+ columns) but is abruptly cropped at the right edge with no fade, arrow, or scroll indicator hinting that more dates exist. Add a subtle edge fade or scroll hint so users know to swipe horizontally.

working_well: Weekend columns (SAT, SUN) get a subtle tinted background, making it easy to scan rest days at a glance.
Room types are grouped with a bold header row followed by their rate-plan sub-rows, giving the dense grid clear hierarchy.
The currently selected date (FRI 31) is highlighted with an underline and brand-orange color, standing out from the rest of the header row.
worth_considering: Consider freezing the first column (room type / rate plan names) so labels stay visible while scrolling horizontally through dates.
Light row dividers or alternating shading within the rate-plan sub-rows could make it easier to track a single row across many date columns.
The rate figures render in a fairly light gray — worth double-checking contrast against both the white and tinted weekend backgrounds.
